claim: A small cluster of cholinergic neurons in the dorsal habenula (dHb) of zebrafish is defined by their expression of the lecithin retinol acyltransferase domain containing 2 a (lratd2a) gene.
source: We identified a small cluster of cholinergic neurons in the dorsal habenula (dHb) of zebrafish, defined by their expression of the lecithin retinol acyltransferase domain containing 2 a (lratd2a) gene and their efferent connections with a subregion of the ventral interpeduncular nucleus (vIPN).
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the identification of these neurons based on lratd2a expression.

claim: The lratd2a-expressing neurons have efferent connections with a subregion of the ventral interpeduncular nucleus (vIPN).
source: We identified a small cluster of cholinergic neurons in the dorsal habenula (dHb) of zebrafish, defined by their expression of the lecithin retinol acyltransferase domain containing 2 a (lratd2a) gene and their efferent connections with a subregion of the ventral interpeduncular nucleus (vIPN).
evidence: The abstract explicitly describes the efferent connections of these neurons.

claim: The lratd2a-expressing neurons in the right dHb are innervated by a subset of mitral cells from both the left and right olfactory bulb.
source: The lratd2a-expressing neurons in the right dHb are innervated by a subset of mitral cells from both the left and right olfactory bulb and are activated upon exposure to the odorant cadaverine that is repellent to adult zebrafish.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the bilateral innervation pattern.

claim: The lratd2a-expressing neurons are activated upon exposure to the odorant cadaverine.

claim: In zebrafish, nine glomerular clusters in the olfactory bulb receive olfactory information from sensory neurons in the olfactory epithelium.
source: In zebrafish, nine glomerular clusters in the olfactory bulb (OB) receive olfactory information from sensory neurons in the olfactory epithelium and, in turn, transmit signals to four forebrain regions: the posterior zone of the dorsal telencephalon (Dp), the ventral nucleus of the ventral telencephalon (Vv), the posterior tuberculum (PT), and the dorsal habenular region (dHb) (Miyasaka et al., 2014; Yoshihara, 2014).
evidence: The introduction explicitly describes the olfactory pathway with citations.

claim: Olfactory bulb glomerular clusters transmit signals to four forebrain regions: Dp, Vv, PT, and dHb.
source: In zebrafish, nine glomerular clusters in the olfactory bulb (OB) receive olfactory information from sensory neurons in the olfactory epithelium and, in turn, transmit signals to four forebrain regions: the posterior zone of the dorsal telencephalon (Dp), the ventral nucleus of the ventral telencephalon (Vv), the posterior tuberculum (PT), and the dorsal habenular region (dHb) (Miyasaka et al., 2014; Yoshihara, 2014).

claim: Only the right nucleus of the dHb is innervated by mitral cells from the olfactory bulb.

claim: lratd2a-expressing neurons are predominantly located in the right dHb.
